- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought overreaction.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast for downside risk.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth 3-day moving average before forecasting.
